children: U.S. Treasury yields extended their sharp rise Thursday, with the benchmark 10-year yield climbing to 5.15% as investors weighed stronger inflation pressures and rising expectations for another Federal Reserve rate hike in October.

The moves followed a sharp selloff in Treasurys on Wednesday, when the 10-year yield jumped 16 basis points to 5.12%, its highest level since July 2007. The rise came as investors sold bonds across the curve amid stronger growth expectations, fresh inflationary pressures, and reduced expectations for near-term Fed easing.

Expectations for an October Fed rate hike also surged past 70% Wednesday following hawkish central-bank commentary and signs of renewed inflation pressure. The market had been pricing a materially higher probability of another increase as investors reassessed the path for monetary policy.

The rise in yields has reflected concern that persistent inflation could keep the Fed tightening for longer. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said more rate hikes were likely needed to quell inflation, pointing to strong demand as well as supply shocks, including higher import and commodity prices, according to a Reuters report.
